title: Turn one virtue into an observable distinction

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Observable virtues are patterns of judgment, not heroic labels. Courage checks and raises a justified concern despite cost; honesty corrects a known falsehood; justice applies relevant standards consistently; temperance governs an optional appetite; compassion notices and responds to suffering; humility acknowledges a limit; loyalty serves a legitimate commitment without deception; patience allows needed time without neglecting urgency; wisdom weighs these goods in context.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: A notice credits Lee alone, although the signed contribution log credits Lee for text and Mo for layout. The owner welcomes private corrections until 16:00. Jo is nervous about seeming difficult but faces no stated retaliation risk. Mo permits correction of the credit, not discussion of private circumstances.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Describe courageous correction, deficiency and excess. Then choose two other virtues from the definitions and specify distinct observable conduct in this same case.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A helper waits politely while an urgent agreed task is being missed, calling this patience. Is waiting necessarily virtuous?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Check the log and request accurate joint credit privately before 16:00. Silence solely to avoid mild awkwardness misses the opportunity; a public accusation of theft exceeds known facts. Honesty preserves actual contributions; humility avoids guessing motive; justice gives neither friend preferential credit. Partial: name virtues without behavior. Next try a different low-stakes situation for one remaining virtue, recording action, competing good and correction from evidence rather than scoring character.
criteria: Virtue is expressed as observable judgment
A label does not replace contextual reasoning

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Patience must fit the need; a timely respectful clarification may better serve the obligation. Neither calm appearance nor immediate intervention proves wisdom without the circumstances.
